correctness.rationale: PASS: For any bounded convex planar Ω, the solution of (Δ−μ²)v=0 with boundary data 1 satisfies 0<v<1. The centered inscribed disk B_d(x) is contained in Ω; its explicit radial comparison b(z)=I_0(μ|z−x|)/I_0(μd) has b=1 on the circle, and the maximum principle gives v(x)≤I_0(μd)^{-1}. Strong maximum principle forces equality only if Ω equals the disk. A supporting line to Ω at a closest boundary point y gives an inward normal distance s with s(x)=d, and φ=e^{-μs} solves the same PDE while φ≤1 on ∂Ω; strict maximum principle gives v(x)>e^{-μd} for bounded Ω. Large tangent disks B_R((0,R)) with x=(0,d) have v(x)=I_0(μ(R−d))/I_0(μR)→e^{-μd}. This proves the exact infimum/supremum and nonattainment at finite R for the stated domain class.

originality.rationale: FAIL: The two-sided envelope is mechanically implied by stronger prior results and standard named comparison principles rather than a new theorem. Nazarov (arXiv:2609.06523v1, Theorem 1) already proves |∇v|≤μv throughout every bounded convex Lipschitz planar Ω, which integrated from the boundary gives v(x)≥e^{-μd}; his Section 3 explicitly constructs the supporting-half-plane exponential barrier and proves V_μ<v_μ throughout Ω, yielding the claimed strict lower inequality at the nearest supporting point directly. Kuznetsov (arXiv:2403.09382v2) records exact half-plane exponential and disk Bessel model solutions. The upper bound is the immediately standard maximum-principle domain comparison with the inscribed disk; the equality case follows automatically by the strong principle, while the lower tangent-disk limit is the standard I_0 asymptotic. The full optimization is a direct recombination of those known comparisons, not a distinct mathematical advance; an absence of matching wording is immaterial.
residual_risks: This FAIL assesses novelty and substantive value of this exact assertion, not the validity of the maximum-principle inequalities.
No theorem is claimed that the exact two-sided envelope was printed in Nazarov verbatim; its implication follows by the explicit steps stated above.
The submitted scope is planar bounded convex Lipschitz domains; no analogous conclusions for nonconvex/higher dimensions are assessed.
